title: Golden Triangle (Delhi–Agra–Jaipur)

itineraries.title: Golden Triangle in 5 days: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur
itineraries.summary: The classic first trip to India at a steady pace: a day in Delhi, the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri on the way west, and two days in Jaipur.
itineraries.seoTitle: Golden Triangle 5-Day Itinerary: Delhi, Agra & Jaipur
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic 5-day Golden Triangle itinerary: Delhi, the Taj Mahal at sunrise, Fatehpur Sikri and Jaipur, with distances, weekly closures and booking tips.

plan.overview: Delhi, Agra and Jaipur form a triangle of roughly 200–270 km per side, so each leg is a half-day by road or a few hours by train. Plan the days around two weekly closures: the Red Fort is closed on Mondays and the Taj Mahal on Fridays (the Gatimaan Express to Agra doesn't run on Fridays either). Starting on a Friday, Saturday, Sunday or Tuesday keeps both open on the right days.

budget.assumptions: Entry fees per adult foreign visitor where an official source lists them (Agra monuments). Delhi and Jaipur monument fees couldn't be confirmed from an official page, so check them before you go. Transport, hotels and meals are not estimated.

booking.detail: Book Delhi–Agra and Jaipur–Delhi trains on IRCTC well ahead in the October–March season.
Buy Taj Mahal and ASI tickets online to save time at the gates.
For the Agra–Fatehpur Sikri–Jaipur leg, a car with driver is the simplest option; agree the price in advance.

alternatives: Short of time? Drop Fatehpur Sikri and drive straight from Agra to Jaipur.
If your dates don't fit, reverse the second half (Delhi, Jaipur, then Agra) so the Taj Mahal doesn't fall on a Friday.
Add a night in Agra to see the Taj at night on full-moon dates.
tips: Check the weekly closures before fixing dates: Red Fort (Mondays), Taj Mahal (Fridays).
Leave food, tripods and chargers in the car on Taj day.
